Tesla booked just $146 million in credit revenue in Q2, down 67% from $439 million a year ago and less than half the $380 million it reported in Q1. It's the lowest in years. And because credits cost Tesla almost nothing to produce, that's near-pure profit walking out the door. This is the drop-off we've been flagging. Credit sales peaked at a record $2.76 billion in 2024, then fell 28% to $1.99 billion in 2025, sliding quarter by quarter: $595 million in Q1 2025, $439 million in Q2, $417 million in Q3, $542 million in Q4. Now they've fallen off a cliff. A year ago, credits added almost two full points to Tesla's gross margin. This quarter, at $146 million, they added barely half a point. The cause is policy. The $7,500 federal EV tax credit expired on September 30, 2025, and a change in federal law zeroed out the penalties automakers pay for missing fuel-economy standards, which was the whole reason rivals bought Tesla's credits. Avatar for Fred Lambert Fred Lambert | Jul 22 2026 - 1:13 pm PT. 81 Comments. Tesla Q2 2026 financial results. Tesla (TSLA) released its financial results and shareholders' letter for the second quarter (Q2) 2026 after market close today. We are updating this post with all the details from the financial results, shareholders' letter, and the conference call later tonight. The earnings call with management is scheduled for 5:30 p.m. ET. ... Tesla's regulatory credits collapse. The clearest driver of that shrinking profit is regulatory credits. Tesla booked just $146 million in credit revenue in Q2, down 67% from $439 million a year ago and less than half the $380 million it reported in Q1. It's the lowest in years. And because credits cost Tesla almost nothing to produce, that's near-pure profit walking out the door. This is the drop-off we've been flagging. Credit sales peaked at a record $2.76 billion in 2024, then fell 28% to $1.99 billion in 2025, sliding quarter by quarter: $595 million in Q1 2025, $439 million in Q2, $417 million in Q3, $542 million in Q4. Now they've fallen off a cliff. A year ago, credits added almost two full points to Tesla's gross margin. This quarter, at $146 million, they added barely half a point. The cause is policy. The $7,500 federal EV tax credit expired on September 30, 2025, and a change in federal law zeroed out the penalties automakers pay for missing fuel-economy standards, which was the whole reason rivals bought Tesla's credits. With that market gone, this line isn't coming back, and Q2 is the first clean look at Tesla's margins without it."}},{"name":"source_title","value":{"stringValue":"Tesla (TSLA) releases Q2 2026 financial results: record revenue, big profit miss | Electrek"}},{"name":"url","value":{"stringValue":"https://electrek.co/2026/07/22/tesla-tsla-q2-2026-financial-results/"}},{"name":"publication_time","value":{"stringValue":"July 22 2026"}},{"name":"byline_age","value":{"stringValue":"6 days"}}]}},{"structValue":{"fields":[{"name":"index","value":{"stringValue":"2.4"}},{"name":"snippet","value":{"stringValue":"Tesla (TSLA) Q2 2026 earnings summary. On one page: record second-quarter revenue of $28.236 billion, up 26% year-over-year, and record Q2 deliveries of 480,126 vehicles — the company's first year-over-year delivery growth in roughly two years. On the next: operating income collapsed 57% to $398 million, non-GAAP EPS missed consensus by roughly 38%, and free cash flow turned negative for the first time since early 2024. The market's verdict arrived fast. TSLA shares closed at $374.01 on July 22, the day of the release, then slid to about $358.53 in after-hours trading as the earnings call got underway.
